title: The Business Foundations Webinar
badge: Four pillars for new entrepreneurs · 60 minutes
promise: Documentation, profitability, stability and adaptability. By the end you hold a one-page Business Foundations Blueprint.

panels.label: Welcome
panels.title: Build the business before the business builds you.
panels.notes: [Smile. Slow.] SAY "Welcome. In the next 60 minutes you will draft the foundation of your business. Cameras on if you can. My team screenshots you, and you get something valuable at the end." [1 min]

panels.label: Where are you from
panels.title: Write your city and your business idea in the chat.
panels.notes: MOVES "Where are you from? Write your city and what you want to build." (10) Read three names out loud and thank each person by name. "Can anybody else relate to starting from zero?" (8) Write RELATE. [2 min]

panels.label: The rules
panels.title: Three rules for the next hour.

cards.title: Bring a pen
cards.body: You will fill in your own blueprint as we go.

cards.title: This is not television
cards.body: Write in the chat. I read everything.

cards.title: An offer is coming
cards.body: At the end I will share one small offer. Take it or leave it.

panels.notes: SAY the rules out loud, slowly. Say the third rule twice. "An offer is coming at the end. Does that sound fair?" (7) Write FAIR. [1 min]

panels.label: The promise
panels.title: You hold your one-page ==Foundations Blueprint==.
panels.notes:
SAY the promise twice in different words. "In 60 minutes you leave with one page that tells you what to write down, what to earn, what to protect and what to adjust." [1 min]
NEED: group photo slide is skipped, add one if you want it.

panels.label: The problem
panels.title: Good ideas die from missing basics.
panels.notes:
SAY "Most new founders spend months on the idea and ten minutes on the basics." Keep it your own voice. "How many of you have started something without writing down the numbers?" (10) Write ME. [1 min]
NEED: add your own credentials in 30 seconds. They are left off the slides until you give me sourced facts (numbers, places, names).

panels.kicker: Earn the Right · the low point
panels.label: The low point
panels.title: I once ran a business on hope.
panels.sub: No records. No margin. No plan B.
panels.notes:
[PAUSE] [Lower your voice. Look into the camera.] SAY your real low moment here in 60 to 90 seconds.
NEED: replace this line with your true story. Keep the slide as it is if it is true for you. [2 min]

panels.label: The decision
panels.title: Keep guessing. Or build the ==foundation==.
panels.notes: SAY "I had two options. I took the second." [1 min]

panels.label: One word
panels.title: Foundation.
panels.notes: MOVES "Foundation. Say that with me." (3) "Write FOUNDATION in the chat." Thank everyone who writes. You can be fast, or you can be what? Solid. (6) [1 min]

panels.label: The four pillars
panels.title: Four pillars hold every business up.

cards.title: 1 · Documentation
cards.body: What is written down is yours.

cards.title: 2 · Profitability
cards.body: Money in must beat money out.

cards.title: 4 · Adaptability
cards.body: Change before you are forced to.

panels.notes: SAY "Four pillars. Learn one, write one line. We do this four times." Hand out: ask them to draw four boxes on a page. [2 min]

panels.kicker: Teach One Win · the hidden cost
panels.label: The hidden cost
panels.title: Why the basics come first.
panels.because: A business without a foundation is a hobby with expenses.
without: No record of what you earned
panels.notes:
SAY the because line slowly. "How many of you recognise one of the left column?" (10) Write LEFT. [1 min]
NEED: add your own cost number (hours or money) only when you have a true one.

panels.label: Pillar 1
panels.title: If it is not written down, it is not yours.
panels.notes: SAY "Writing it down is how you own it, protect it and hand it over." [1 min]

panels.label: The four papers
panels.title: Four papers every new business needs.

cards.title: Legal basics
cards.body: Registration, licences and tax number where you live.

cards.title: Simple agreements
cards.body: Who delivers what, by when, for how much.

cards.title: Money records
cards.body: Invoices, receipts, a separate business account.

panels.notes: SAY each paper in one sentence. Remind them: rules differ by country, so check your local registry and a local accountant. The fifth section of a process note is the check: how do you know it worked? "If you do a task three times, write it down." "Does that make sense?" (7) [3 min]

panels.label: Your turn 1
panels.title: Which paper do you not have yet?
panels.sub: Write it in box 1 of your page.
panels.notes: SAY "Three minutes. Write the one paper you will create this week." Wait in silence. Then: "Write DONE in the chat when your line is written." (5) [3 min]

panels.label: Pillar 2
panels.title: Revenue is a number. ==Profit== is a decision.
panels.notes: SAY "You can be busy, loved and broke at the same time." [1 min]

panels.label: The formula
panels.title: Pay yourself ==first==, then spend.
panels.notes: SAY "Take a small percentage of every sale into a separate account first. Live on the rest." Do not give tax or legal advice; tell them to confirm with a local accountant. "If you only have the rest, you find a way." [3 min]

panels.label: Three numbers
panels.title: Know these three numbers.

cards.title: Gross margin
cards.body: What each sale keeps after its direct cost.

cards.title: Break-even
cards.body: Sales you need each month to cover fixed costs.

cards.title: Cash on hand
cards.body: Profit on paper is not money in the bank.

panels.notes: SAY "Break-even equals your monthly fixed costs divided by the margin on one sale." Example (illustrative, say so): fixed costs 1,000, margin per sale 50, break-even is 20 sales. "Quizzer: break-even is how many sales? 20." (5) [4 min]

panels.label: Your turn 2
panels.title: Write your break-even in box 2.
panels.sub: Fixed costs divided by margin per sale.
panels.notes: SAY "Three minutes. A rough number is fine. Write the number in the chat only if you want to." Thank everyone who shares. [3 min]

panels.label: Pillar 3
panels.title: Build so one bad month is a ==bruise==, not a break.
panels.notes: SAY "Growth gets the attention. Stability keeps you in business." [1 min]

panels.label: Four protections
panels.title: Four things that keep you standing.

cards.title: A cash cushion
cards.body: Start with one month of costs. Build toward three.

cards.title: More than one client
cards.body: No single customer should be your whole income.

cards.title: Systems, not you
cards.body: If you are sick, the work still ships.

cards.title: A money rhythm
cards.body: Daily glance, weekly check, monthly review.

panels.notes: SAY each in one sentence. Money rhythm: 60 seconds daily on balances, 20 minutes weekly, 60 minutes monthly, 3 hours quarterly. "You can be right, or you can be... ready." (6) [4 min]

panels.label: Your turn 3
panels.title: Which protection are you missing most?
panels.notes: SAY "Two minutes. One protection. One first step." [2 min]

panels.label: Pillar 4
panels.title: Your plan will be wrong. Be ready to ==change== it.
panels.notes: SAY "Not if. When. The winners are not the ones who guess right. They are the ones who adjust fast." [1 min]

panels.label: The 90-day loop
panels.title: Review, decide, test small, repeat.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: Look at the numbers and the feedback.

steps.title: Test small
steps.body: One small experiment, not a big bet.

panels.notes: SAY "Every 90 days, sit down and ask four questions." "What worked? What did not? What will I change? What will I stop?" [3 min]

panels.label: Wake up
panels.title: Which pillar is your weakest today?
panels.notes: MOVES "Which pillar is your weakest? Write 1, 2, 3 or 4." (10) Read the count out loud and thank people by name. Tie back: "This is why we need all four." [2 min]

panels.label: Your blueprint
panels.title: Your one-page Foundations Blueprint.

items: 1 · One paper to create this week

panels.lede: Read your page out loud to yourself. That is the win.
panels.notes: SAY "Read your four lines out loud. That page is worth more than most business plans." "Write DONE if you have four lines." (5) [3 min]

panels.label: Permission
panels.ask: Would it be okay if I shared a small offer with you?
panels.notes: SAY "Thank you for staying. Would it be okay if I shared a small offer?" (1) Wait. Thank each person who writes OK by name. [1 min]

panels.label: Two paths
panels.title:
You can keep guessing.
Or you can build it ==properly==.
panels.notes:
SAY "Business owners who wing it, write 1. Business owners who want a system, write 2." (split the room) [2 min]

panels.title: What if your whole foundation was built for you in a week?
panels.notes: [Slow down. This is the turn.] SAY "That is why I created this." [1 min]
